title: Saʿd ibn Yūsuf comes of age at sixteen and takes the government into his own hands. The regency of Naṣr al-Istijjī ends
Naṣr al-Istijjī, regent for barely half a year, dies on the very day the young sultan comes of age. The court gives out that it was 'sickness'; the game records a hunting accident
source: save of 11 September 1364 (died 18 January 1364, hunting accident); Trent's account ('sickness')

title: Sultan Saʿd takes a second wife: Duʿāʾ of the Marīnid house, twice widowed, his father's widow and minister. He comes to the throne with two wives, Aiman the Mamlūk and Duʿāʾ the Marīnid
source: Trent's account (after Naṣr's death on 18 January 1364; exact date not given)

title: A Portuguese army of 4,200 falls on the Valencian host at Cañete and breaks it: 1,100 of the 2,400 men of Balansiyya are lost, for 300 Portuguese
The ṭāʾifas of Balansiyya and Mursiyya attack the joined armies of Portugal and Aragon at Castellón de la Plana and are thrown back: 2,800 against 7,600, and 1,200 lost for 340
The ʿulamāʾ are displeased with the young sultan: their satisfaction stands at 37% in the middle of the war

Saʿd summons the Jamāʿa and brings in reforms for the ʿulamāʾ. The tax on the dhimmīs, remitted since 1352, is collected again, and a new campaign of conversion begins. It is enough to keep the clergy from mutiny while the war goes on
Granada is drawn in as an ally when the Mamlūks go to war with Cilicia

After chasing it halfway across Iberia, the Granadan army under Murād catches the joined host of Portugal and Aragon at Zafra, in Castilian land held by the Marīnids, and breaks it: 9,800 against 6,750, and 3,350 of theirs lost for 2,200 of ours
Before the walls of Lisbon the Granadan army destroys the Portuguese remnant of Zafra: all 1,620 killed or taken, for none of ours
The next day, at Lisbon again, the Aragonese remnant is destroyed in its turn: 1,770 killed or taken, for none of ours

The realm's people are quickly going back to their Andalusī roots. Andalusīs are now 54% and Castilians 40%, where in March 1359 the two had been nearly equal. In faith the realm is still split, 302,000 Sunnī to 291,000 Catholic
The treasury holds 522, but the deficit remains (income 55 against expenses 94 a month). The ʿulamāʾ stand at 47% and the dhimmīs, taxed again, at 66%, down from 84%

Portugal is dealt with first. On the day its last army is destroyed before Lisbon it makes a separate peace and gives up its south: thirteen towns of the Algarve and the lower Alentejo, from Silves and Faro to Beja and Mértola, with 83,000 people. The court means to make them a new vassal state once the war is won

data.plan: release as a vassal after the war

source: autosave of 1 July 1365 (Portugal left the war on 11 September 1364; the thirteen towns are Granada's); Trent's account

title: In the gulf of Valencia an Aragonese squadron attacks the Valencian fleet and is beaten off
Aiman the Mamlūk bears Sultan Saʿd his first child, a daughter, Umm al-Fatḥ, 'mother of victory'
